mechanism: Amphotericin B causes nephrotoxicity and electrolyte disturbances (hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia) that increase phenytoin toxicity risk and reduce seizure control; phenytoin may also induce metabolism of amphotericin B.
action: Monitor serum phenytoin levels, renal function, and electrolytes closely; maintain phenytoin levels in therapeutic range (10-20 mcg/mL); correct electrolyte abnormalities promptly; consider alternative antifungal if possible.
